purpose: Register the latest high-fidelity document/image restoration and text-preserving super-resolution research discovered after the previous global search. These are research candidates and benchmark references only.

newResearchCandidates.name: TAIR / TeReDiff
newResearchCandidates.notes: ICLR 2026 text-aware diffusion restoration; SA-Text and Real-Text resources; explicitly addresses textual fidelity and warns that severely degraded text may remain unrecoverable.

newResearchCandidates.name: TiGeSR
newResearchCandidates.notes: CVPR 2026 two-stage strategy: restore glyph structure first, then enhance the image; third-party base models/datasets remain separately licensed.

newResearchCandidates.name: TADiSR
newResearchCandidates.notes: 4x real-world SR with text-aware cross-attention and joint text-mask decoding; released adapters remain subject to base-model licenses, including commercial-use terms.

newResearchCandidates.name: TADSR
newResearchCandidates.notes: CVPR 2026 one-step diffusion SR candidate; current release still depends on separate checkpoints and external datasets, so it remains research-only until rights and reproducibility are cleared.

newResearchCandidates.name: RGDiffSR
newResearchCandidates.notes: Recognition-guided diffusion SR; uses recognizers and model checkpoints that must each be rights-checked. Useful as a glyph/recognition-aware comparator.

newResearchCandidates.name: RTSRN
newResearchCandidates.notes: Text-image SR baseline from ACM Multimedia; useful for recognition-aware benchmark comparison.

newResearchCandidates.name: TATT
newResearchCandidates.notes: CVPR 2022 text-attention SR designed for spatial deformation robustness; useful for warped or curved page/text crops.

newResearchCandidates.name: DocRes
newResearchCandidates.notes: Unified document restoration for dewarping, deshadowing, appearance, deblurring, binarization and end-to-end processing.

newResearchCandidates.name: DocNLC
newResearchCandidates.notes: Document enhancement over blur, noise, shadow, watermark and background degradations.

newResearchCandidates.name: DeQA-Doc
newResearchCandidates.notes: VQualA 2025 DIQA championship method; useful as an independent quality assessor rather than a restoration engine.

newResearchCandidates.name: DIQA-5000
newResearchCandidates.notes: 5,000 enhanced document images with human MOS for overall quality, sharpness and color fidelity; useful for validating restoration pipelines.

newResearchCandidates.name: Nautilus-OCR
newResearchCandidates.notes: National Library of Luxembourg pipeline for enhancement prediction and OCR reprocessing of original METS/ALTO packages, with side-by-side visual comparison. Repository notes a mix of open-source libraries and some proprietary contributions.

newResearchCandidates.name: NDNP-Open-OCR
newResearchCandidates.notes: Library of Congress open pipeline creating ALTO/PDF at scale from historical scans; includes advanced segmentation and local deployment. Third-party software obligations remain separate.

newResearchCandidates.name: DiffHDR / HDR28K
newResearchCandidates.notes: Historical document repair with 28,552 damaged/repaired image pairs and character-level annotations; directly relevant to archival degradation research.

newResearchCandidates.name: SwinIR
newResearchCandidates.notes: Official repository supports super-resolution, denoising and compression-artifact reduction; include upstream Swin Transformer/KAIR license review as required.

newResearchCandidates.name: NAFNet
newResearchCandidates.notes: Efficient restoration baseline; suitable for conservative deblur/denoise before OCR. A CoreML port documents edge artifacts under reduced precision, reinforcing precision-aware benchmarking.

newResearchCandidates.name: HYPIR
newResearchCandidates.notes: Strong research restoration candidate but current official distribution explicitly restricts commercial use without permission.

newResearchCandidates.name: SUPIR
newResearchCandidates.notes: High-end restoration research system but current official distribution has a non-commercial-only condition.

newResearchCandidates.name: ScanTailor Advanced
newResearchCandidates.notes: Mature deterministic scan cleanup, binarization and layout preparation. Useful complement to neural restoration where reproducibility is valued.

newResearchCandidates.name: LA-DocFlatten
newResearchCandidates.notes: Layout-aware flattening with explicit warning that dataset terms differ from code terms.

promotionCriteria: Register every candidate without making it a runtime dependency.
Keep immutable source images and bitstreams untouched.
Benchmark on Arabic books and manuscripts before generic image benchmarks can influence promotion.
Measure OCR-CER/WER, glyph topology and diacritic preservation in addition to PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/DISTS.
Reject restoration that improves visual quality while introducing false characters, dots, diacritics or historical details.
Separate engine, checkpoint, base-model, dataset and third-party component rights.
Use deterministic and generative pipelines side-by-side on identical pages.
Keep 24K-class output as a delivery target, never as evidence that missing historical detail was truly recovered.
